# `.length` on a map, run on three backends.
#
# The checker typed `.length` as int on a list or a string and let it through
# on a map as an unchecked `dyn` select, so each backend spelled whatever it
# spelled for a field: Go's `len(m)` happened to be right, JavaScript read
# `m.length` off a `Map` (undefined -- the property is `size`), Kotlin emitted
# `m.length`, which does not compile, and the interpreter looked the map up for
# a key named "length". The list half is here too, because the interpreter had
# no `.length` select at all and failed it for a list as well.

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'
! stdout 'FAIL'

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'
! stdout 'FAIL'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'
! stdout 'FAIL'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:test"
import . "sngl:ui"

output {
    none {
        html
    }
}

component counts node {
    var stock map[string, int] = {"a"=1, "b"=2}
    var xs = [1, 2, 3]
    var mapLen = 0
    var listLen = 0

    button #go(text="go", @click {
        mapLen = stock.length
        listLen = xs.length
    })
}

func testLength(t Test, c counts) {
    c.go.click()
    t.assert(c.mapLen == 2)
    t.assert(c.listLen == 3)
}

window {
}
